description: This donut chart visually compares the distribution of deception outcomes across two distinct ambiguity categories, labeled “Ambiguity 1 (Outer)” and “Ambiguity 2 (Inner)” in separate legends. The chart is composed of two concentric rings, each divided into three colored segments corresponding to the categories “Deceived” (red), “Partially” (yellow), and “Not Deceived” (green), as defined in their respective legends. The outer ring, representing Ambiguity 1, shows a red segment labeled 67.6%, a yellow segment labeled 57.9%, and a green segment labeled 10.5%. The inner ring, representing Ambiguity 2, shows a red segment labeled 31.6%, a yellow segment labeled 23.5%, and a green segment labeled 8.8%. Each percentage value is printed directly within its corresponding colored segment. The chart does not include a single legend for both rings; instead, it uses two separate legend boxes, one for each ambiguity level, to map the colors to their respective categories. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order around each ring, with the largest segment (red, 67.6%) appearing at the top left of the outer ring.
